verdict.rationale: Keycloak documents built-in SCIM endpoints per realm for managing users/groups (enabling SCIM, service account client setup) which supports directory-driven user/group sync ([kc-supp-scim]), and it also supports LDAP/AD federation and IdP brokering for directory integration ([keycloak-docs-8], [kc-supp-federation]). However, the evidence never explicitly describes an end-to-end deprovisioning-on-delete flow or shows independent/hands-on confirmation that SCIM-driven removal actually revokes app sessions/access. Missing for 10: explicit deprovisioning behavior documentation, independent/hands-on validation of SCIM sync working with a real customer directory, and details on real-time propagation of revocation to connected apps.
